case_title.correct_value: Suresh Kumar v. State of Haryana
case_title.quote: SURESH KUMAR v STATE OF HARYANA
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment heading.

number_of_accused.quote: Appellant-accused alongwith his mother was prosecuted
number_of_accused.reason: Husband and mother-in-law were both prosecuted, so two accused.

accused_gender.reason: The accused is the husband, referred to as he throughout.

accused_age.reason: The judgment gives no age for the accused; 28 has no textual basis.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.correct_value: Army personnel (serving in the Army, not permanently at matrimonial home)
accused_occupation.quote: Since Suresh Kumar was in the Army, he was not permanently staying in the matrimonial home
accused_occupation.reason: The judgment states the accused was in the Army, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status is not discussed in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: The deceased Sulochana is the wife, a woman.

victim_age.reason: The judgment gives no age for the deceased; 28 is not supported.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: The appellant Suresh Kumar married Sulochana on 18th February, 1990
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused was the husband of the deceased.

offence_category.quote: such death shall be called 'dowry death'
offence_category.reason: Charges were under s.304-B IPC dowry death with s.498A.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC s. 304-B, s. 498A; Evidence Act s. 113-B
statutory_provisions.quote: offences punishable under Section 498-A and Section 304-B of the IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Both IPC sections are correctly listed; s.113-B Evidence Act is also central but omitted.

weapon.reason: No weapon is mentioned; death was by electric shock or electrocution.

evidence_type.correct_value: Oral testimony of witnesses (PW-4, PW-5, PW-7, father); judgment does not characterise evidence as circumstantial
evidence_type.quote: This has come out in the evidence of Gian Singh, Mam Chand, Sardha and PW-7 Beer Singh.
evidence_type.reason: Judgment relies on direct witness testimony; 'circumstantial' is never stated.

confession.reason: No confession by the accused is recorded; his s.313 statement denied nothing about electrocution.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Demand for dowry (motorcycle), cruelty and harassment, beating despite intervention
aggravating_circumstances.quote: He had subjected her to cruelty or harassment in connection with the demand by beating her
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Dowry demand, cruelty and harassment are the aggravating facts relied on.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating circumstances are discussed in the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.quote: Trial Court acquitted both the accused.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: Acquittal reversed; convicted under s.304-B and s.498A
high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court reversed the acquittal and held him guilty
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court reversed acquittal and convicted the accused.

final_outcome.quote: We find no merit in these appeals and they are accordingly dismissed.

offence_finally_established.correct_value: Dowry death (s.304-B IPC) and cruelty (s.498A IPC)
offence_finally_established.reason: Dowry death under s.304-B was established and upheld.

imprisonment_type.quote: rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years

imprisonment_years.quote: rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years under Section 304-B
imprisonment_years.reason: Seven years under s.304-B is stated.

fine_rs.quote: rigorous imprisonment of three years along with a fine of Rs.5,000/-
fine_rs.reason: Rs.5,000 fine is stated, attached to the s.498A sentence.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Facts without stating the lower-court outcomes or the finding that the accused failed to rebut the presumption
neutral_facts.quote: The High Court reversed the acquittal, finding that the victim's death was a dowry death
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate but reveal the High Court's conviction outcome and rebuttal finding, which should be omitted.

offence_severity.correct_value: Imprisonment not less than seven years, may extend to life
offence_severity.quote: shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life
offence_severity.reason: Matches the statutory punishment text in s.304-B(2).

physical_harm.quote: the deceased is said to have died of an electric shock or electrocution
physical_harm.reason: Death by electrocution is described as the cause.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Two offences (s.304-B and s.498A), both upheld
number_of_offences.quote: The correctness of the appellant's conviction for an offence punishable under Section 498-A and Section 304-B
number_of_offences.reason: Two offences charged and both convictions upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property loss is discussed; dowry demand concerns a motorcycle but no loss is claimed.

motive.quote: Suresh Kumar demanded a motorcycle as dowry
motive.reason: Dowry demand for a motorcycle is the motive.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Court accepted the dowry demand for a motorcycle and cruelty/harassment; electrocution was only 'said to have' occurred and was not accepted as proved
key_evidence_accepted.quote: Sulochana is said to have died of an electric shock or electrocution
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court accepted the dowry demand and cruelty; it did not accept electrocution as established.

witness_credibility.correct_value: Trial judge discarded Gian Singh's testimony; High Court accepted prosecution witnesses on demand and cruelty; arrival-time discrepancy held irrelevant
witness_credibility.quote: While there is some discrepancy in the time of their arrival ... this seems to us to be not quite relevant
witness_credibility.reason: Summary omits trial judge discarding Gian Singh and the court's treatment of discrepancies as irrelevant; partly accurate.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Body cremated before victim's family arrived; accused did not mention electrocution in s.313 statement
post_offence_conduct.quote: they came to know that Sulochana had already been cremated
post_offence_conduct.reason: The judgment records cremation before family arrived and omission of electrocution in s.313 statement, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

custody_duration.reason: Duration of custody is not quantified; only set-off under s.428 is mentioned.

bail_history.correct_value: Bail bond cancelled; accused directed to be taken into custody to serve remainder of sentence
bail_history.quote: The bail bond of Suresh Kumar is cancelled and it is directed that he should be taken into custody
bail_history.reason: Judgment states the bail bond was cancelled, so bail history is stated.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: None noted (FIR delay argument raised late and rejected)
procedural_irregularity.quote: We also do not see any adverse consequence or presumption in the delay
procedural_irregularity.reason: FIR delay contention was rejected as raised late; no irregularity found.

trial_duration.correct_value: Trial court judgment 3 October 1996; High Court 25 March 2008; Supreme Court 11 November 2013
trial_duration.reason: Dates match the judgment's stated decision dates.

legal_representation.correct_value: R.C. Kohli, S.S. Shamshery, Bhakti Vardhan for Appellant; Kamal Mohan Gupta, Rajeev Gaur Naseem, Mohd. Zahid Hussain, Naresh Bakshi for Respondent
legal_representation.quote: R.C. Kohli, S.S. Shamshery, Bhakti Vardhan for the Appellant.

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR lodged 19 Sept 1993; Suresh Kumar arrested 19 Sept 1993; mother Leela Devi arrested 20 Sept 1993
investigation_status.quote: Suresh Kumar was arrested on the same day while his mother Leela Devi was arrested on 20th September, 1993
investigation_status.reason: The 20 September arrest was of the mother, not the accused; otherwise accurate.

appeal_history.correct_value: Trial court acquittal; High Court reversed and convicted; Supreme Court dismissed appeal
appeal_history.quote: his acquittal was reversed and he was convicted of the offences charged

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Prosecution case reflected in High Court reasoning; judgment does not expressly record prosecution submissions on s.113-B
prosecution_argument.quote: The High Court held that the ingredients of Section 304-B of the IPC were made out
prosecution_argument.reason: Content reflects the High Court's reasoning, not explicitly recorded prosecution arguments; attribution is inferred.

defence_argument.correct_value: High Court should not have interfered with acquittal; death was accidental; prosecution should have produced doctor
defence_argument.quote: it was submitted that if two views are possible, the High Court should lean in favour of the accused
defence_argument.reason: Defence contentions on acquittal interference, accidental death and the doctor are recorded.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Initial burden on prosecution; reverse onus on accused to prove death accidental
legal_principle_applied.quote: a reverse onus is put on the accused to prove his innocence by showing, inter alia, that the death was accidental
legal_principle_applied.reason: Matches the principle stated in para 48.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Also Shamnsaheb M. Multtani, Yashoda, Nallam Veera Stayanandam, Sharad, Pathan Hussain Basha, Hira Lal, Ghurey Lal, S. Anil Kumar, Rohtash
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Shamnsaheb M. Multtani vs. State of Karnataka (2001) 2 SCC 577
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Listed cases are correct but the list omits many precedents relied on, including Multtani and Ghurey Lal.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Not stated as a sentencing rationale; judgment gives conviction reasoning only
sentencing_rationale.quote: The High Court held that the ingredients of Section 304-B of the IPC were made out
sentencing_rationale.reason: Conviction reasoning is accurate, but the judgment gives no sentencing rationale; the value conflates the two.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors were identified by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Not stated as formal sentencing factors; court described accused as unrelenting in insisting on dowry
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: Suresh Kumar was unrelenting and insisted on a motorcycle being given by way of dowry
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court described accused as unrelenting and insisting on dowry, so 'None' is inaccurate.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: Seven years rigorous imprisonment under s.304-B; three years rigorous imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine under s.498A; concurrent; s.428 CrPC set-off
other_sentence_order.quote: The sentences were directed to run concurrently
other_sentence_order.reason: Sentence details and concurrency match the judgment.
